title: VAPT Auto-Heal Implementation Contract v2.0
description: Machine-readable contract governing auto-heal quality and consistency fixes across all VAPT bundle files. v1.0 incorrectly stated 27.3% rollback coverage — the actual coverage is 100% for structured rollback objects and 100% for disable actions. The real work is fixing consistency gaps, not filling coverage voids. This contract defines 8 phases to resolve marker collisions, sync cross-file rollback data, fill null remove_operations, and resolve legacy string mismatches. It extends (not replaces) vapt_platform_contract_v3.0.json.

audit_corrections.description: Coverage numbers from v1.0 contract were based on a flawed analysis. This section documents the corrected findings from the comprehensive re-audit.

interface_schema_disable_actions.note: All 133 risks have disable actions at actions[] level. 68.8% have concrete remove_operation at platform_implementations level; 31.2% have null remove_operation but all have disable_driver_ref

pattern_library_structured_rollback.note: All 430 entries have rollback_structured field. 118 also have legacy rollback string; 312 have only rollback_structured

litespeed_action_field.claimed: 8 steps missing action field in rollback
litespeed_action_field.actual: All 8 litespeed rollback objects already have action=remove_block
litespeed_action_field.real_bug: 4 of 8 have same-file marker collision with htaccess enforcer (not missing action)

root_causes_of_v1_errors: Interface_schema uses actions:[{type:'enable'},{type:'disable'}] array, not actions:{enable:{},disable:{}} dict — parser expected dict and found zero disable keys
Enforcer_pattern_library has two rollback fields: legacy 'rollback' (string, 118/430) and 'rollback_structured' (object, 430/430) — analysis only saw the string field
Driver_manifest rollback objects were all present — the 312 'missing' count was based on counting only legacy rollback strings in pattern_library, not actual driver_manifest entries

stakeholder_context.objective: Fix auto-heal consistency gaps — the system is structurally complete (100% rollback, 100% disable actions) but has cross-file inconsistencies, marker collisions, null remove_operations, and legacy string mismatches that undermine auto-heal reliability

auto_heal_definition.enable_flow: Feature ON -> Check idempotency -> Backup -> Inject wrapped_code (with markers) at insertion_point -> Verify injection -> On failure, auto-rollback
auto_heal_definition.disable_flow: Feature OFF -> Locate begin_marker in target_file -> Regex-remove marker block -> Verify removal (disable_verification) -> On failure, restore from backup
auto_heal_definition.core_principle: Every protection that can be injected MUST be removable by a corresponding, symmetric, marker-based operation — no orphaned code, no partial states, no cross-enforcer marker collisions

known_gaps: 4 LiteSpeed steps have same-file marker collision with htaccess enforcer (RISK-013, 023, 024, 035)
32 Cloudflare rollback_structured in pattern_library have rule_identifier=null (driver_manifest has full API details)
22 wp_config entries in pattern_library have semantic mismatch between legacy rollback string and rollback_structured
134 platform_implementations have remove_operation=null (all have disable_driver_ref as fallback)
118 pattern_library entries have legacy rollback string; 312 do not (inconsistent presence)
8 LiteSpeed steps use apachectl -t for verification (Apache-specific, not LiteSpeed)

target_state.remaining_limitation: Cloudflare rollback_structured in pattern_library will be synced from driver_manifest but actual execution still requires runtime API credentials

structural_preservation_rule.description: The JSON schema/structure of all existing bundle files is IMMUTABLE. Auto-heal implementation may only modify content within the existing structure — never change the structure itself. Exception: marker values may be changed (e.g., # BEGIN VAPT RISK-013 -> # BEGIN VAPT LS RISK-013) to fix collisions, but the field names and object shapes remain unchanged.
rules: Top-level keys must NEVER be renamed, removed, or reordered
The nesting hierarchy must remain identical — new fields are added as siblings at the appropriate level
Value types must be preserved — strings stay strings, objects stay objects, arrays stay arrays
Existing fields may have their VALUES changed (e.g., marker strings, null -> concrete value) but field names must not change
New fields (e.g., remove_operation where currently null) must follow the naming conventions already established in each file
rollback_structured objects in pattern_library must follow the existing schema: {action, begin_marker, end_marker, target_file} for file-based, {action, rule_identifier, note} for Cloudflare

rollback objects in driver_manifest must follow the existing schema: {action, begin_marker, end_marker, target_file} for file-based, {action, rule_identifier, zone_id, api_endpoint, api_method, auth_required} for Cloudflare
The contract file (vapt_autoheal_contract_v2.0.json) is a NEW file with its own independent structure and is not bound by this rule
JSON formatting style (indentation, key ordering conventions) must match the source files

marker_system_reference.description: The marker system is the foundation of auto-heal. Every injected protection block is wrapped in platform-appropriate comment markers for reliable identification and removal. LiteSpeed enforcers now get their own distinct marker prefix to prevent same-file collision with htaccess enforcers.

litespeed.rationale: LS prefix prevents same-file marker collision when litespeed and htaccess both write to .htaccess

php_functions.rationale: PF prefix prevents same-file marker collision when php_functions and wordpress enforcers both write to vapt-functions.php

cloudflare.note: Cloudflare uses API-based rule management, not file markers. Rollback requires DELETE API call.

litespeed_marker_change.old_format: # BEGIN VAPT RISK-XXX / # END Of RISK-XXX
litespeed_marker_change.new_format: # BEGIN VAPT LS RISK-XXX / # END Of LS RISK-XXX
litespeed_marker_change.collision_description: For these 4 risks, both htaccess and litespeed enforcers write to {ABSPATH}.htaccess with identical markers. The litespeed idempotency check would find the htaccess marker and skip, preventing LiteSpeed protection from being applied. Rolling back either enforcer would remove the other's block.
litespeed_marker_change.non_collision_note: These 4 litespeed steps also write to {ABSPATH}.htaccess but the corresponding htaccess step targets a different file (e.g., wp-content/uploads/.htaccess). Still, using distinct LS markers is consistent and prevents future collisions if file targets change.

marker_system_reference.wordpress_convention_alignment: Mirrors WordPress core # BEGIN WordPress / # END WordPress pattern

php_functions_marker_change.old_format: // BEGIN VAPT RISK-XXX / // END Of RISK-XXX
php_functions_marker_change.new_format: // BEGIN VAPT PF RISK-XXX / // END Of PF RISK-XXX

collision_pairs.RISK-126: WordPress Core + PHP Functions in vapt-functions.php
collision_pairs.RISK-133: WordPress Core + PHP Functions in vapt-functions.php

php_functions_marker_change.collision_description: For these 12 risks, both WordPress/WordPress Core and PHP Functions enforcers write to the same vapt-functions.php file with identical markers. The PHP Functions idempotency check would find the WordPress marker and skip, preventing PHP Functions protection from being applied. Rolling back either enforcer would remove the other's block.

phase_1.title: Critical Fix — LiteSpeed Marker Collision Resolution
phase_1.description: 4 LiteSpeed enforcer steps (RISK-013, 023, 024, 035) share identical markers with their corresponding htaccess steps in the SAME target file ({ABSPATH}.htaccess). This causes: (1) litespeed idempotency check finds htaccess marker and skips, so LS protection never applies; (2) rollback of either enforcer removes the other's block. Fix: change all 8 litespeed steps to use '# BEGIN VAPT LS RISK-XXX' / '# END Of LS RISK-XXX' markers. This change must be made consistently across 3 files: driver_manifest, pattern_library, and interface_schema.

phase_4.title: Pattern Library — Fix wp_config Legacy Rollback String Mismatches
phase_4.description: 22 wp_config entries in enforcer_pattern_library have a semantic mismatch: the legacy 'rollback' string says 'wp config delete <CONSTANT>' (which deletes the constant entirely, including pre-existing ones) while rollback_structured says 'remove_block' with marker-based removal (which only removes the VAPT-wrapped block). This creates ambiguity about which behavior is intended. This phase updates the legacy rollback strings to align with the safer marker-based semantics of rollback_structured.

actions.description: For each of the 22 wp_config entries with mismatched rollback string, update the legacy rollback string to describe marker-based removal instead of wp-config-delete
actions.after_template: Remove /* BEGIN VAPT RISK-{NNN} */ ... /* END Of RISK-{NNN} */ block from wp-config.php
actions.rationale: The rollback_structured action is 'remove_block' with markers — the legacy string should describe the same operation. wp config delete would remove a pre-existing constant that VAPT merely wrapped, causing data loss. Marker-based removal only removes VAPT's additions.
